title: Looking for demo and trailer feedback. Barista Boom: A cozy, hands-on coffee making game.
author: Rcraft
selftext:
Hi everyone! This is my first time sharing this game I've been building. \[Free demo live here\]( [https://play.runcheygames.com/baristaboom](https://play.runcheygames.com/baristaboom))

It's a cozy, hands-on coffee making game. You adventure around your island and others, assembling a peculiar crew of helping hands, and work increasingly intricate barista jobs. You also solve mysteries and get to play a variety of minigames (briefly, and skippable!)

![gif](cdr9f5cr790i1 "You'll make a latte of these")

At this stage, I'm really hoping to get feedback from others here on the gameplay trailer and the demo experience, particularly the tutorial and early pacing. I put a few friends through the intro levels to make sure they could follow it, so it's \*at least\* sensible. Does the gameplay trailer clearly convey what the game offers? Is the game actually fun and/or charming?   
  
BTW - the game isn't built to run on a phone. The UI elements become a bit too small. It does work well on the Steam Deck however. A big enough phone might work, but it's not recommended.

Please \[check out the demo\]([https://play.runcheygames.com/baristaboom](https://play.runcheygames.com/baristaboom)) if the game seems interesting to you. There are more screenshots on the \[game's main page\]([https://runcheygames.com/barista-boom](https://runcheygames.com/barista-boom)) as well if you want to learn more about the game before committing to a demo or if you're on mobile and can't play this minute.

I put up some \[longer gameplay\]([https://youtu.be/IBRjlspftBQ](https://youtu.be/IBRjlspftBQ)) footage from later in act 1, too. 

If anyone has questions about my development process, I'm happy to answer them. In a nutshell I've been hammering away at this in a terminal with claude-code for a bit more than a month as a full-time thing. I don't use any asset packs or generators or libraries like three.js, the systems have just been purpose-built for what the game needed at the time as far as I know (I don't look at the code).

comments.author: s3v3nt
comments.body: Honestly, it looks chaotic. There is far too much going on in each scene to understand what is happening. Also, what is going on? What was that Pokemon fight sequence?? And then some kind of judge thing near the end... I'm really confused on what this is trying to be.

replies.author: Rcraft
replies.body:
Thank you for the feedback! I can see the chaos of it, it's hard to step back and realize that I'm so used to seeing things fly around that they don't register. I should definitely... find some simpler scenes to make it seem clearer up front. And those weird fight sequences and judge things - yea, they just seem out of pocket vs. "hey there are minigames here too".

I also probably need to actually add \*some\* text to the trailer to explain it, or cut it if I can't express it without text and let it show up in the game.

replies.author: Rcraft
replies.body:
https://reddit.com/link/1xqgtwj/video/3q5c5t2ki90i1/player

I love AI - so easy to cut up new trailers. I cut out all of the extraneous silliness from the first trailer and tried to really slow down the action to show how a player would control the game.
